title: Security & Compliance Review - Pen Test and Vulnerability Management
summary: Redwood and Atlas reviewed latest pen test findings, remediation timelines, vulnerability management processes, secure SDLC practices, and patching cadence. Discussed SOC 2/ISO controls alignment, RBAC/SSO integration, audit log retention, KMS/encryption, and evidence Redwood can provide for Atlas procurement. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share pen test report summary, vulnerability SLA, and SOC2 attestation; schedule technical follow-up to validate audit logging and KMS integration details.
action_items: Avery Chen: Send redacted pen test summary + remediation plan; due 2025-02-18
Diego Morales: Share architecture diagram showing KMS integration and audit log pipeline; due 2025-02-19
Priya Patel: Provide SOC 2 Type II report and ISO scope doc; due 2025-02-17
Evan Ruiz: Confirm Atlas legal info for data residency requirements and follow-up meeting availability; due 2025-02-20
next_steps: Redwood to email redacted pen test findings and timeline for open items
Schedule 60-min technical deep dive (SE-led) to validate audit log hooks and KMS key ownership
Customer to share minimum encryption/KMS controls and SOC2 evidence checklist
Agree on an acceptable patching cadence for critical CVEs (48-72h target) and non-critical (monthly)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-02-12 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52 minutes | Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood CSM); Evan Ruiz (Atlas CISO), Maya Singh (VP Eng), Tom Becker (Cloud Security), Ruth Lee (Compliance)

Summary: quick run through of pen test, vuln mgmt and SDLC. Some audio artifacts, speaker overlaps, minor transcription errors expected.

[00:00] Avery Chen: all right good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. this is Avery from Redwood, with Diego and Priya. Evan, Maya, thanks for making time. purpose today is to walk through the pen test results and our vulnerability management & patching cadence that you asked about.

[00:24] Evan Ruiz (CISO): thanks. our procurement team asked for a short walk-through and we need to understand timelines--critical for our compliance sign-off. we also want to validate how you manage keys and audit logs.

[00:45] Diego Morales (SE): yeah hi. i'll take the tech bits. quick note, the pen test was done by an external 3rd party in Dec 2024 and we did a follow-up internal triage in Jan. i'll outline findings and remediation status, and then we can deep dive into KMS, logs, and patching cadence.

[01:12] Maya Singh (VP Eng): before we get too deep — can you confirm whether Redwood retains KMS keys or if we can integrate with our customer-managed KMS? that's a hard req for us.

[01:30] Diego Morales (SE): good question. we support BYOK for our Private deployment via a customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS/HSM). for Hosted API customers we manage keys by default but we offer a dedicated key option for Enterprise contracts. i can share the architecture diagram after this call.

[01:52] Ruth Lee (Compliance): and what about audit logs retention? our legal require 7 years for certain transaction traces, and we need to know retention, immutability, and export options.

[02:10] Priya Patel (CSM): i can share our logging policy doc — we currently retain standard audit logs for 13 months by default in the hosted offering; for Dedicated/Private we can configure longer retention and export to customer S3 or SIEM. immutability via WORM and obj lock is possible on a per-contract basis.

[02:35] Tom Becker (Cloud Security): ok good. let's go into the pen test findings. what were the highest severity items and what's the patching cadence been like?

[02:51] Diego Morales (SE): summary: five high severity findings, mostly around misconfig on an internal admin endpoint that could expose metadata; we patched that within 48 hours after discovery. two medium findings tied to dependency versions on non-user facing components — remediated in the following weekly release.

[03:15] Evan Ruiz (CISO): can you point to an evidence artifact for the 48h remediation? we need timestamps and PR IDs for our audit team.

[03:28] Avery Chen: yes we'll provide a redacted timeline and the PR/issue IDs. we usually produce a pen test summary (redacted) + remediation log for customers under NDA.

[03:40] Maya Singh: who owns ongoing vuln mgmt? do you have a centralized program and SLAs for triage? we need to know how we escalate critical CVEs.

[03:55] Diego Morales: we have a central Security Ops team that ingests vuln feeds (NVD, vendor notices), runs an internal risk score, and assigns to owners via JIRA. SLA: critical (CVSS >= 9) targeted patch within 48-72 hours, high within 7 days, medium monthly, low per quarterly. that SLA is part of our Enterprise playbook.

[04:23] Evan Ruiz: 48-72 is reasonable. do you do active exploit assessments or just patch testing?

[04:35] Diego Morales: we do both. for criticals we run targeted exploit verification in a staging environment prior to prod deployment. we also run regression tests and smoke tests.

[04:50] Ruth Lee: how does that integrate with your secure SDLC — i.e., do you require dependency scanning and code reviews before merge?

[05:02] Diego Morales: yes, we use SCA tools (we use Snyk and a combination of OSS scanning) in CI; PRs block merges on certain policy failures. we also have mandatory peer review and security sign-off for services touching customer data.

[05:20] Maya Singh: any fuzzing or fuzz testing on the runtime? given you're running LLMs, memory safety and nginx/engine boundaries are important.

[05:33] Diego Morales: we have fuzzing in our CI for critical libs and run ASAN builds for native components nightly. for the inference runtime we run additional memcheck and leak detection during release candidates.

[05:50] Evan Ruiz: back to KMS — if we use BYOK, who rotates keys and how is access audited?

[06:05] Avery Chen: for BYOK, customers control key rotation. Redwood stores references but does not have plaintext access to customer keys if BYOK is enabled. audit logs show key usage events and we can stream those to your SIEM.

[06:22] Tom Becker: what about SSO / RBAC — we need SCIM provisioning + SAML SSO and granular roles.

[06:33] Priya Patel: we support SAML/SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and granular RBAC roles (admin, dev, reader, billing). for Dedicated/Private we can add custom roles.

[06:48] Maya Singh: is RBAC enforced at the request routing level or only at the console? we need API-level enforcement.

[07:00] Diego Morales: API-level enforcement. tokens are scoped and evaluated against RBAC at the gateway layer; we have tracing hooks so you can see which principal invoked what model and token counts per principal.

[07:15] Evan Ruiz: let's talk about audit trails — retention, tamper evidence, and ability to export per-request logs with model, prompt hash, response length, latency.

[07:28] Diego Morales: per-request logs are available. by default we keep detailed traces for 30 days, aggregated metrics for 13 months. for Enterprise we can configure log streaming to your S3 or SIEM for longer retention and provide signed log digests for tamper evidence.

[07:48] Ruth Lee: signed digests — can you elaborate? do you sign with an internal key or can we verify with a public key?

[07:58] Diego Morales: we produce SHA-256 digests and sign them with our platform key; we can provide public verification keys under NDA. for the most stringent customers we support HSM-backed signing.

[08:14] Maya Singh: about data residency — we need EU-only hosting and contractual guarantees about no cross-region replication. how do you handle that?

[08:26] Avery Chen: we have region pinning and data locality controls. for Hosted, EU region ensures data stays in region; for Dedicated/Private you can host in your VPC and have full control. we'll provide contractual language for data residency.

[08:43] Evan Ruiz: good. we also want to understand your patching cadence for base OS images in the inference fleet — do you use immutable images, and what's the typical window from patch release to rollout?

[08:58] Diego Morales: we use immutable AMIs/OCI images for nodes, and a canary rollout model. critical kernel/security patches are packaged as hotfix images and can be rolled within 48-72 hours after QA. routine OS updates follow a monthly maintenance window.

[09:15] Tom Becker: what about third-party dependencies of models (tokenizers, transformers libs)? how do you manage CVEs there?

[09:26] Diego Morales: we track dependency manifests, rely on SCA and automated PRs for upgrades. critical CVEs in libraries used by inference runtime trigger immediate patch cycles and coordinated deployments. we also maintain a whitelist of vetted runtime libs.

[09:40] Ruth Lee: on pen test specifics — you said five high sev; any remnants open or deferred?

[09:49] Diego Morales: two high sev items were fully closed; three were mitigated with compensating controls and scheduled for an architectural fix in the next release (ETA 2025-03-05). we documented risk acceptance where immediate fix would cause customer impact.

[10:05] Evan Ruiz: can you share the compensating controls and risk acceptance rationale? our audit team will want that.

[10:14] Avery Chen: yes we'll include descriptions in the redacted report along with mitigation steps and timelines.

[10:22] Maya Singh: i want to drill into vuln SLAs — do you publish a public vulnerability disclosure and do you have a bug bounty?

[10:32] Diego Morales: we have a public vuln disclosure policy and run a private bug bounty via a platform for high-value customers. we also accept responsible disclosure via our security@ address.

[10:45] Evan Ruiz: about secure SDLC evidence — do you provide attestations or artifacts (e.g., CI policy, SCA dashboard exports, test coverage) for procurement?

[10:57] Priya Patel: we can provide a package of artifacts under NDA: SOC 2 Type II attestation, secure SDLC checklist, SCA scan summary, CI gating policy, and change control logs.

[11:14] Tom Becker: let's talk SLA on vulnerability response — will you sign an SLA that maps CVSS to time-to-patch in the contract?

[11:25] Avery Chen: for Enterprise contracts we can include vulnerability response commitments tied to severity. typical language mirrors our internal SLA but we are willing to discuss contract terms.

[11:38] Maya Singh: do you support signed images and reproducible builds so we can verify images before deployment?

[11:47] Diego Morales: yes — we sign images and can provide build provenance. for Dedicated/Private we can share CI provenance artifacts so you can verify hashes.

[12:00] Evan Ruiz: deep dive needed on audit logging: we want to ensure prompt-level data isn't retained longer than required and that logs are redacted for PII. how do you handle prompt storage vs telemetry?

[12:18] Diego Morales: prompts for hosted customers are retained per contract; we support masking and prompt hashing for telemetry. we separate telemetry (latency, token counts) from full prompt storage. for customers with strict requirements we can configure prompt retention to zero and only store prompt hashes and minimal metadata.

[12:40] Ruth Lee: how do you handle legal holds? customer may need preserved data for litigation — can you place holds and export the relevant artifacts?

[12:52] Priya Patel: yes we support legal hold workflows in Dedicated and Private; for Hosted we handle on a case-by-case basis with legal review. exports can be delivered to your S3 under encryption.

[13:08] Maya Singh: on incident response — what's your RCA timeline and third-party notifications for breaches?

[13:19] Diego Morales: incident comms: internal detection within 24 hours, customer notification within 72 hours for confirmed breaches, full RCA within 30 days. we have runbooks and a security on-call rotation.

[13:35] Evan Ruiz: is that in your SOC2 controls?

[13:40] Priya Patel: yes, incident response and monitoring are covered in SOC2 scope. we'll send the SOC 2 Type II report which includes those control descriptions.

[13:50] Avery Chen: quick checkpoint — any burning items you want us to expand on today?

[13:58] Maya Singh: i'd like the follow-up technical deep dive on KMS and audit logs. also need the redacted pen test summary.

[14:07] Evan Ruiz: and the vulnerability SLA and evidence package. procurement needs those to move forward.

[14:15] Diego Morales: we'll prepare a 60-min SE-led demo showing KMS key flows, audit log exports, and sample signed digests.

[14:27] Ruth Lee: can you include a sample contract clause for data residency and key ownership?

[14:34] Avery Chen: yes legal can provide suggested language; we'll attach to the package.

[14:40] Tom Becker: small nit — do you patch your GPU driver stacks separately? those often carry remote exploit vectors.

[14:49] Diego Morales: yes GPU drivers are managed via our infra team; we deploy driver updates in a controlled window with canaries. critical driver CVEs follow the same 48-72 hour SLA if they affect security posture.

[15:05] Maya Singh: great. on the pen test, can you confirm the scope (prod vs staging)?

[15:15] Diego Morales: the test targeted staging and our internal admin plane; no live customer data in scope. we'll indicate the scope in the redacted report.

[15:26] Evan Ruiz: for compliance, we need assurance that any mitigations that are compensating controls are timeboxed and tracked in a register we can audit. do you have a remediation register?

[15:39] Diego Morales: yes we maintain a remediation register with statuses, owner, PR references, and target dates. we'll include an export for audit.

[16:00] Priya Patel: action items recap: we'll send the pen test summary, SOC2 report, architecture diagram, and remediation register.

[16:14] Maya Singh: timeline for docs? we need them by next week ideally.

[16:20] Avery Chen: we'll aim to deliver the package by 2025-02-18.

[16:26] Evan Ruiz: scheduling the deep dive — availability next Tues/Wed?

[16:33] Diego Morales: i'm available next Wed 15:00 UTC for a 60-min SE deep dive.

[16:39] Ruth Lee: works for us. Evan will confirm.

[16:45] Avery Chen: perfect. final question — any specific compliance frameworks beyond SOC2/ISO you need us to address?

[16:52] Ruth Lee: PCI not relevant; just SOC2 and ISO plus data residency and legal hold capability.

[16:58] Maya Singh: and we want the SLA language for vuln response in the contract.

[17:05] Avery Chen: noted. we'll include proposed SLA language.

[17:12] Evan Ruiz: thanks team. that's all from me.

[17:20] Priya Patel: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with the package and a calendar invite for the deep dive.

[17:28] Meeting end: 52:00.

Notes on transcription quality: there are a few mis-hearings in proper nouns and some speaker attribution artifacts — please refer to the attachments we will send for canonical artifacts.
